title: arXiv Biology & Biomedicine — Wednesday, 11 November 2026
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this is a relevance-ranked selection rather than a measured popularity ranking. Its biomedical coverage is incomplete, with much experimental and clinical preprint activity appearing on bioRxiv and medRxiv.

sections.title: Headline
sections.text: Nine notable papers from the latest available arXiv announcement batch (Wednesday, 11 November). The dominant pattern is computational molecular design increasingly paired with biochemical experiments, alongside computational advances in genomics, single-cell analysis, and imaging uncertainty. This is a relevance-ranked selection, not a measured popularity chart: arXiv has no official trending chart, and its biomedical coverage is incomplete—much experimental and clinical preprint activity appears on bioRxiv and medRxiv. The requested day is Thursday, 12 November; at the 01:17 UTC snapshot no Thursday batch was listed, so this report uses the prior Wednesday batch.
sections.global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this is a relevance-ranked selection rather than a measured popularity ranking. Its biomedical coverage is incomplete, with much experimental and clinical preprint activity appearing on bioRxiv and medRxiv.

sections.title: Emergent Biological Capabilities in a Foundation Model for Molecular Interactions
sections.abstract: Bonbon learns protein–ligand interaction representations and the authors report zero-shot molecular-function predictions plus prospective biochemical hit validation across nine targets.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors claim one frozen sequence-only model supports mechanism, binding-site, and bond-type predictions; their prospective assays yielded a 61.5% dose-response hit rate among the tested de novo compounds.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: NeurIPS 2026 main-track oral status is independently listed by NeurIPS; the authors report a prospective assay panel spanning nine disease targets and seven protein families.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper says its interaction distinctions are still coarse and it does not recover explicit 3D coordinates. Biochemical target hits are not evidence of clinical safety or efficacy.

sections.title: ProTEUS: A mutation-resolved world model for closed-loop protein evolution
sections.abstract: ProTEUS combines mutation-effect prediction with experimental feedback to guide protein engineering; the authors report two closed-loop enzyme campaigns producing variants with over tenfold wild-type activity.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors connect sequence, evolutionary, and structural representations to mutation actions, and describe a physics-constrained structure predictor and feedback loop for steering protein evolution.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Listed in the 11 November biomolecules batch; the paper reports closed-loop wet-lab work on two enzymes, aldehyde dehydrogenase and levansucrase, in addition to mutation-prediction benchmarks.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported engineering campaigns cover two enzyme targets and assay-specific activity outcomes; they do not establish broad transfer to other protein classes or organism-level effects.

sections.title: Bridging Graph and Pairwise Learning for Gene Regulatory Network Inference from scRNA-seq Data
sections.abstract: scGPL combines whole-network topology with local transcription-factor/target-gene pair learning and reports improved benchmark performance across seven single-cell datasets.
sections.claimed_contribution: The method fuses global regulatory-graph features with dynamically sampled local subgraphs to address weaknesses of graph-only and pairwise-only inference.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The arXiv record says accepted to Bioinformatics; the authors report seven benchmark datasets, a maximum 13.7% gain over their strongest baseline, and code plus versioned data releases.
sections.unique_caveat: These are computational network-inference benchmarks, not experimental confirmation of regulatory edges. The authors note dynamic subgraph sampling adds computational overhead.

sections.title: ANTIOCH-VS: From Sequence to Hits with Modular, Open-Source Ensemble Virtual Screening
sections.abstract: ANTIOCH-VS builds receptor ensembles from sequence and ranks candidate ligands; on two retrospective target benchmarks, its top-20 lists were enriched for known binders.
sections.claimed_contribution: The pipeline combines conformational ensembles, docking, consensus ranking, and metadynamics triage to screen from a protein sequence without a ligand-bound crystal structure.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The authors provide an open-source end-to-end workflow and report tests on JAK2 and ADRB2 DUD-E sets, with top-20 hit rates of 20% and 60% respectively (random selection about 1–2%).
sections.unique_caveat: Both evaluations are retrospective computational benchmarks; enriched shortlists are not prospective biochemical hits or evidence of therapeutic efficacy.

sections.title: Detection of local recombination and mutation hotspots in bacterial genomes using neural posterior estimation
sections.abstract: A simulation-trained neural posterior estimator models gene-level bacterial mutation and recombination rates and propagates uncertainty into hotspot detection.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors use neural posterior estimation conditioned on a fixed clonal genealogy, then a circular posterior-propagated detector to identify local rate hotspots.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper combines simulation recovery tests with applications to three bacterial datasets (Bacillus cereus, Staphylococcus aureus, and Escherichia coli) and provides a public Python implementation.
sections.unique_caveat: The inference is conditional on the specified recombination model and genealogy; the data applications illustrate use but do not experimentally validate hotspot function or fitness effects.

sections.title: Pyrite: Building and Benchmarking Protein-Ligand Pose Ranking Agents
sections.abstract: Pyrite benchmarks protein–ligand pose ranking and compares expert chemists with language-model agents that reason over poses or discover features for a classical ranker.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report up to 67% accuracy for direct reasoning and 74% for LLM-guided feature construction, above the observed expert performance on this benchmark.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The benchmark contains 1,500 pose pairs and is listed for the Agentic AI for Biological Discovery workshop at NeurIPS 2026; Semantic Scholar’s indexed record showed zero current citations and zero influential citations at this snapshot.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported accuracy is benchmark-specific and computational; it does not establish pose correctness or binding experimentally. The evaluation uses a held-out post-AF3 split after training on earlier benchmark data.

sections.title: When Covariance Is Not Enough: Kernel-Based Regularization for Single-Cell Counterfactuals
sections.abstract: The authors add a nonlinear independence penalty to single-cell counterfactual models and report better recovery of known edits in simulations and improved expression-profile generation on one scRNA-seq dataset.
sections.claimed_contribution: The paper argues that linear cross-covariance penalties can miss nonlinear dependence and uses normalized HSIC to regularize the separation of known and unknown factors.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The work pairs controlled simulations with a real single-cell RNA-seq application; the indexed Semantic Scholar record showed zero current citations and zero influential citations at the snapshot.
sections.unique_caveat: The real-data test is one dataset and the counterfactual profiles are model outputs, not observed responses to matched perturbation experiments.

sections.title: Improved Myelin Water Fraction Estimation and Uncertainty Mapping in Multicomponent T2 Relaxometry via NNLS Bootstrap Aggregation
sections.abstract: NNLS-BB bootstraps repeated non-negative least-squares reconstructions to estimate myelin water fraction and signal-perturbation variability, improving simulation error and scan–rescan measures in small healthy cohorts.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report 36–41% lower mean absolute error than conventional NNLS in simulations and lower regional scan–rescan dispersion in both cohorts.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The study compares against four alternatives on 40,000 simulated voxels and assesses repeatability in two independent cohorts totaling 13 healthy participants.
sections.unique_caveat: The in-vivo repeatability sample is small and limited to healthy participants; it does not establish performance in neurological disease or clinical diagnosis.

sections.title: A first application of split conformal prediction for dose prediction in knowledge-based radiotherapy planning
sections.abstract: Split conformal prediction is used to form patient-level uncertainty intervals for deep-learning radiotherapy dose estimates, with empirical coverage assessed on head-and-neck cases.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report empirical coverage near nominal levels, with maximum aggregation more conservative and quantile aggregation producing narrower intervals.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper applies patient-level split conformal constructions to a deep ensemble and compares maximum, quantile, groupwise, and locally scaled intervals; the arXiv comment says it was submitted to Physics in Medicine & Biology.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract does not state the cohort size, and empirical calibration in the reported head-and-neck setting is not external clinical validation; finite-sample guarantees depend on the conformal sampling assumptions.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
sections.text: Protein design and ligand ranking are being tested across a prediction-to-assay spectrum. ProTEUS and Bonbon report wet-lab activity experiments, whereas ANTIOCH-VS and Pyrite evaluate virtual screening or pose-ranking benchmarks. These are complementary tasks, not four independent validations of a single pipeline. Genomic and single-cell papers focus on recovering structure from sparse observations: scGPL combines global and local regulatory-network information, the recombination-hotspot paper estimates gene-level rates with uncertainty, and the kernel counterfactual paper tests nonlinear dependence penalties. Imaging methods make uncertainty more explicit in myelin-water measurements and radiotherapy dose predictions.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
sections.text: Test protein predictions prospectively and independently: replicate ProTEUS and Bonbon assay findings across broader protein panels with blinded preregistration, matched baselines, and independent labs; test Pyrite and ANTIOCH-VS against experimental structures and prospective binding assays. Ground genomic and single-cell predictions in perturbations: evaluate scGPL and counterfactual expression on held-out Perturb-seq or CRISPRi data, and test bacterial hotspot calls across independent lineages. Measure imaging transfer beyond development settings: assess NNLS-BB and conformal coverage in larger diseased cohorts, across scanners and institutions, with distribution shifts represented.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.text: The clearest evidence-rich thread is protein modeling linked to experimental assays, while the genomics and single-cell papers mostly make computational predictions that still need perturbational checks. Imaging papers add uncertainty estimates, but their reported evaluation settings are not broad enough to imply clinical readiness. This is a snapshot of one arXiv batch, not a guide to the broader biomedical literature.
